title: Angular velocity expression
description: Essential: The student must correctly derive and state ω₀, e.g., √[G(M+m)/(R+r)³] or an equivalent form.

title: Distances from μ
description: Essential: The student must correctly identify the distances from μ to M and to m as R+r, and from μ to the center of mass as √(R² + Rr + r²).

title: Force balance reasoning
description: Important: The solution should apply centripetal force balance to the two-body system (M and m) or to μ to find ω₀.

title: Geometry application
description: Important: The student must correctly apply geometric relations (e.g., law of sines/cosines) to find distances in the equilateral configuration.

title: Perturbation analysis setup
description: Important: For part (3), the student must set up the energy or force equation for μ and introduce a small radial perturbation.

title: Oscillation frequency result
description: Essential: The student must correctly derive the angular frequency of small oscillations as (√7/2)ω₀ for the M=m case.

title: Relative speed calculation
description: Essential: For part (4), the student must compute the relative speed between two spacecraft, obtaining approximately 996 m/s.

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Penalize sign errors in force equations, incorrect square roots, or missing units in final numerical answers.

title: Conserved quantity misuse
description: Pitfall: Penalize incorrect application of angular momentum conservation for μ in part (3), or misidentifying the conserved quantity.

title: Extra geometric insight
description: Optional: The solution may note the equilateral triangle symmetry or use vector methods for relative velocity.
